summary: T023 holdout event completed as a RED with a to-the-byte diagnosis, per the packet's blocked-on-RED ruling. The frozen engine composed and applied a changeset (84 scanned / 8 app + 3 workspace changed, tslint.json removed, 3 unhandled, 8 declared differences); the migrated install was refused at dependency resolution, so no build ran. The @angular/http question is answered No: the public seam passed every reading gate with a real @angular/common@16.2.12 surface and refused all 6 modules on call shape. Five gaps itemised (G1-G5), capability composition mapped, hop-class findings named. Freeze intact, tsc/lint/tests green, no chase, no hand edits, no commits.
open_questions: G1/G2 (install, blocking): the Angular 16 cell has read no line for @ng-bootstrap/ng-bootstrap or preboot, so alignAngularPackageManifest carries them at their era pins and says nothing — neither appears in changes, declaredDifferences or unhandled. @ng-bootstrap/ng-bootstrap@3.1.0's peer @angular/common ^6.1.0 refuses npm outright. Does the boundary want (a) two community-layer registry readings, or (b) the general transform: report any era-pinned declaration the cell has read no line for as unhandled, so silence stops being the failure mode?

G3 (source, the measured question): the frozen engine cannot carry @angular/http. succeedRemovedEntryPointSymbols passed every reading gate and refused all 8 symbol sites because DocumentedSymbolSuccessor states an arity and accepts only call-position uses; every @angular/http symbol here is a type reference, a `new` target, a constructor parameter type or an NgModule imports array member. The missing capability is a value-position, cross-package successor with a use-position classifier and a per-position substitution rule, plus a no-successor refusal for JsonpModule (HttpClientJsonpModule is not a rename). Should that capability be cut as a T024 unit?

G5 (install): AngularMigration.removedFiles names only tslint.json; the changeset never declares the era package-lock.json superseded, so the first install is refused on the era build-angular 0.7.5 pin. The lane applied the pigallery2/super-productivity precedent (move it out, retain byte-identical at target/logs/era-package-lock.json). Should supersession become a changeset declaration rather than a lane convention?

G4 (build): no frozen capability reads npm scripts, so scripts.build:prod stays `ng build --prod --aot --extract-css` while the workspace migration removed the matching extractCss — the workspace and its own driver command now disagree. Is a script-surface retarget capability in scope?

Unmeasured by construction: nothing behind the install refusal was reached, so no TypeScript-construct, template or RxJS-operator gap class is named for the 2.9.2 -> 5.1.3 and 6.2.2 -> 7.8.0 hops. Answering G1/G2 is the only way to measure them.
